newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian dollar more solidly based-RBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian dollar more solidly based-RBA.

text.p: The Australian dollar is more solidly based than it was 10 years ago and is becoming less sensitive to fluctuations in commodity prices, said retiring Reserve Bank governor Bernie Fraser in Tokyo.

"With inflation at low levels, the budget moving towards balance, substantial structural change achieved and the prospect of more to come, the Australian dollar today looks to be more solidly based than it did a decade ago," Fraser said.
Speaking at a BZW conference in Tokyo, and likely to be his last speech before stepping down, Fraser said the dollar will, and should, continue to respond to funamental factors.

These included cyclical changes in commodity prices and interest rate differentials, but it can also be expected to be more stable in the face of other pressures thn it was ten years ago, Fraser said.
However, as a bi-product of export diversification, "Australia's terms of trade are becoming less senstive to fluctuations in commodity prices," he said.
Fraser said the gradual decline in the share of commoditity exports also raises the prospect of less volatility in the exchange rate.
"This could be a significant change for long-term investors, although it has not yet been widely perceived in foreign exchange markets, Fraser said.

Fraser noted that in the area of trade exports of goods and services as a share of GDP had grown to 20.0 percent from 16.0 percent in the last 10 years, while the share of rural and other commodities had declined to 58 percent of total exports from 74.0 percent.
"Significantly, these fluctuations over the past decade have been around a flat trend," he added.
